solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective in the presence of monarch put off

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A police officer was discouraged when the sovereign was watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the presence of' only places the two pieces side by side; it does not signal one going inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to put them off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ravager — I'll skip shattered desire about old defeated city

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the city
shattered means broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
skip means the letter I is left out of desire

parts.note: the I of I'll is the letter that skips
Troy is the ancient city that fell to the Greeks

explanation.surface: A ravager drops his broken longing to go round a fallen ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll skip' drops the I, 'shattered' rearranges the rest as DESER, and 'about' wraps it round the city. A destroyer is also a warship, fitting the military surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wrecks and lays waste is a wrecker; a warship of this name was so called for wrecking enemy vessels.

clue.text: Unseating leader stems negotiations

indicators.note: unseating the leader means removing the first letter of the word for stems

parts.note: stems of plants are stalks

explanation.surface: Ousting the boss halts the bargaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stems' looks like a verb meaning halts; it is the plant parts, minus their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal discussions between parties are negotiations.

clue.text: Chapter on sex in pukka reading

indicators.note: in says the pair goes inside the word for pukka

parts.note: pukka means genuine, real

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the chapter letter above the sex word

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A chapter about sex given a proper reading aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks the chapter letter over the sex word and 'in' sets them inside. Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A public reading of poetry or a passage is a performance of it.

clue.text: Go with a kitty — one of twins on the table?

definitions.text: one of twins on the table?

parts.note: go in the sense of energy or vim is pep
a, as in 'so much a head', is per
a kitty is the pool of money staked, the pot

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go along with a cat, followed by a riddle about twins at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat but is the betting pool. Salt and pepper shakers come as a matched pair, hence 'twins on the table'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaker for ground spice usually sits beside its salt partner, a matching pair on the dining table.

clue.text: Pressure rising in choice brew of Getafix?

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, moves the pressure letter up the word for choice

parts.note: a choice is an option
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure builds over the choice of a druid's concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' lifts the P one place up OPTION. Getafix is the druid in the Asterix comics who brews the magic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Getafix brews a magic drink giving superhuman strength, a liquid concoction of this kind.

clue.text: Mean a lot being one who thrives on (or off) another

definitions.text: one who thrives on (or off) another

parts.note: par is the average or mean level
a lot of land is a site

explanation.surface: Being stingy matters a lot to a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as stingy, but it is the average, par.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism or person living off a host without giving back is a sponger or leech.

clue.text: Fancy soaking up last bit of sun? It's easy to get

indicators.note: soaking up says the cake takes in the letter

parts.note: a fancy is a small iced cake, such as an eclair

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of sun

explanation.surface: A cake soaking up the last of the sun is easy to grab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb; it is a fancy cake. 'soaking up' puts N, from 'last bit of sun', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A message sent in plain language, not coded, is easy for anyone to understand.

clue.text: Bromide allowance covered by platoon's leader

indicators.note: covered by, in a down clue, puts the allowance word beneath the letter
the leader of platoon's is its first letter

parts.note: latitude is freedom or allowance

explanation.surface: An army sedative ration is supervised by the platoon commander.
explanation.walkthrough: A bromide looks like the sedative once dosed to soldiers; here it is a trite remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a trite, unoriginal remark, a cliché.

clue.text: Translator dying to be all over Twitter, Instagram, etc

definitions.text: to be all over Twitter, Instagram, etc

parts.note: dying is an end, the end of life

explanation.surface: A translator is desperate to be talked about across social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dying to' reads as desperate to; 'dying' is END and 'to' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic that is popular all over social media at a given moment is said to be doing this.

clue.text: Court player provided with rightful gold

parts.note: provided (that) can be expressed as so, as in 'so long as'
rightful means lawful, licit
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A tennis player is backed with gold that is legitimately theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court player' suggests tennis; it is a lawyer appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer of this kind acts for clients in legal proceedings, so plays a part in court.

clue.text: Charlie fell for the latest thing

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to fell a building is to raze it to the ground

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie was taken in by the newest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell for' reads as 'was smitten by', but 'fell' is a verb meaning demolish and 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived enthusiasm everyone suddenly follows is a fad, the newest fashion.

clue.text: Stir too fancy a dish

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters of the two words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: give the pot an extra-elaborate stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns STIR TOO into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian rice preparation, cooked slowly in stock, is a well-known dish.

clue.text: Bread is thrown for gull or some such

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Crumbs are tossed to a gull or similar bird at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' is the anagram signal; 'is' only links fodder to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is an example of a bird of the coast and ocean.

clue.text: Perennial is unknown beforehand

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
beforehand means in advance, early

explanation.surface: A plant that returns each year is something we cannot know in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' looks like a plant noun, but here it is the adjective meaning recurring each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring every twelve months, like an annual event, is perennial in the sense of returning regularly.

clue.text: Down under article rewards gripping lyric

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: gripping says the rewards hold the lyric inside them

parts.note: tips are small rewards
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A down-under feature rewards a gripping song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' looks like an adjective praising the lyric, but it is the containment signal. 'Down under' is not the down-clue position but Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Down Under' is slang for Australia and New Zealand, the lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: Move to prompt returning items which support cavalry

parts.note: to move slightly is to stir

indicators.note: returning means the word for prompt is read backwards

parts.note: to prompt is to urge on, to spur

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir up some returning items that help mounted soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives RUPS from the prompt word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse riders rest their feet in these loops hanging from the saddle, which help keep mounted troops steady.

clue.text: Son chuckling is best

parts.note: chuckling is laughter

explanation.surface: A proud remark that a son's giggling is the best thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' reads as an adjective, but it is a verb, to beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce a rival is to beat them heavily, informally to slaughter them.

clue.text: For Parisians very change is a sin in the eyes of the church

definitions.text: a sin in the eyes of the church

parts.note: très is French for very
to pass from one state to another is to change

explanation.surface: To the French, a very big change counts as sinful in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Parisians very' takes the French word très. The Lord's Prayer asks forgiveness for our trespasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Church language in the Lord's Prayer uses this word for a sin or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Piffle a Conservative is spinning

parts.note: piffle means nonsense, rot
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political jibe: what a Tory says is nonsense, all spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' sounds like political spin, but it is the definition: turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning round an axis, like a wheel, is a rotary or revolving motion.

clue.text: Audience engaged in that place

indicators.note: in says the engaged word sits inside the word for that place

parts.note: that place is there
engaged at something is 'at it', so at

explanation.surface: An audience absorbed in what is happening over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal. 'Audience' looks like listeners, but the whole house watching a play can be named after the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole house watching a play can be called by the name of the venue, as in the house rose to applaud.

clue.text: Brownie, for example, drew near artist

parts.note: to draw near is to approach, came
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A young Girl Guide approached a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brownie looks like a junior Girl Guide; it was a cheap Kodak box model taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie was a popular inexpensive box model for taking photographs, an example of the device.

clue.text: What's on some 'eads? Stop emergency procedure

parts.note: hair grows on heads; with the h dropped Cockney-style, as in 'eads, it is 'air
to lift a ban is to stop it

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks what grows on heads, then shouts stop in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of ''eads' tells the solver to drop the h of hair too, a Cockney-accent convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying in supplies or evacuating people by aircraft is a classic emergency operation.

clue.text: Hunter clubs bears — hang on a minute!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
bears means holds or has
er is the hesitant sound someone makes when pausing

explanation.surface: A hunter with clubs and bears tells us to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals; it is the verb, to have.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pursues prey or quarry is a pursuer, a hunter.

clue.text: Put out description of retired reporter?

parts.note: ex means former, so retired
the press stands for journalists, here a reporter

explanation.surface: A former journalist, now retired, is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'description of' just introduces the two parts: an ex-press man is a retired reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a feeling or idea in words is to voice it, to state it.

clue.text: Ecstasy with district's antelope

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a district, an area or region, is land

explanation.surface: A drug turns up alongside a local deer-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "district's" is the possessive, read as 'with the district's'.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African grazing animal with spiral horns is a kind of antelope.

clue.text: Rushing around quietly doing what cartoon angels do

indicators.note: around says the rushing word goes round the quiet letter

parts.note: to hare is to rush, so rushing is haring
P, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: Rushing about, then quietly copying angels in cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts P inside HARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartoon angels sit on clouds plucking a stringed instrument, so they spend their time playing it.

clue.text: Furious as appropriate page is ripped out

indicators.note: ripped out says the page letter is removed from the word for appropriate

parts.note: to pirate a work is to appropriate it illegally

explanation.surface: Someone is livid that a page has been torn from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Very angry is a direct synonym of furious.

clue.text: Go over motor, the focus of auction

parts.note: an Audi is a German car, a motor

indicators.note: the focus is the centre, so the central letter of auction is taken

explanation.surface: Inspect the car that is the centrepiece of the sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the focus of' picks the middle letter of the seven-letter 'auction'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over accounts carefully is to inspect or examine them officially.

clue.text: Who would tear into fool and trouble social worker?

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to trouble is to ail
ants are social insects, and the worker is a class of ant

explanation.surface: Who would lay into an idiot and harass a welfare officer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is the one who tears into a victim.

clue.text: I would back English poet, one to give out

indicators.note: back says the contraction of I would is turned round

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd
Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: I'd return to a poet of England, one who hands things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ID to DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that issues soap, cash or tape is a device that gives it out.

clue.text: Some would say his (or her) term for next successor

indicators.note: some speakers run these two words together so they are heard as one

parts.note: the full term for the one next in line includes the definite article, the; the next successor to an estate or throne is the heir

explanation.surface: A note on usage: the word for the next in line, said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some would say' signals the sound: 'the heir', with the H dropped, sounds like the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural possessive is used as a gender-neutral singular, standing for his or hers.
